questions.question: Substances that have a fixed shape and volume and are virtually incompressible are:
questions.explanation: Solids are rigid substances with fixed shape and volume and are almost incompressible.

questions.question: Solids with a regular, repeating 3D arrangement of atoms are called:
questions.explanation:
Crystalline solids have atoms arranged in a regular, repeating 3D pattern called a crystal
lattice.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a crystalline solid?
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride is an ionic crystalline solid with a well-defined cubic structure.

questions.question: Crystalline solids are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Crystals have a sharp melting point because all bonds break at nearly the same energy.

questions.question: Physical properties that vary with direction are called:
questions.explanation: Anisotropy means physical properties change with direction in a crystal.

questions.question: Solids with many small crystals are:
questions.explanation: Polycrystalline solids are made of many small crystals called grains.

questions.question: Boundaries between grains are called:
questions.explanation: Grain boundaries are the regions where different crystal orientations meet.

questions.question: Polycrystalline materials behave as:
questions.explanation: Random orientation of grains makes bulk materials behave isotropically.

questions.question: Amorphous means:
questions.explanation: Amorphous means “without form” or lacking a regular structure.

questions.question: Glass is often called:
questions.explanation: Glass behaves like a supercooled liquid rather than a true crystal.

questions.question: Amorphous solids have:
questions.explanation: Amorphous solids have only short-range order.

questions.question: Glass-transition temperature is:

options.B: Transition from hard to rubbery state

questions.explanation: Glass transition temperature is where amorphous solids change from hard to rubbery.

questions.question: Natural polymers include:
questions.explanation: Natural polymers include rubber and cellulose.

questions.question: Smallest repeating unit of crystal is:
questions.explanation: The unit cell is the smallest repeating unit of a crystal lattice.

questions.question: Imaginary framework of crystal is:
questions.explanation: A space lattice is the regular arrangement of points in a crystal.

questions.question: Number of crystal systems is:
questions.explanation: There are seven crystal systems in total.

questions.question: Cubic system relation is:
questions.explanation: Cubic system has all sides equal and all angles 90 degrees.

questions.question: Most unsymmetrical system is:
questions.explanation: Triclinic system has unequal sides and angles not equal to 90 degrees.

questions.question: Graphene is made of:
questions.explanation: Graphene is made of carbon atoms in a hexagonal lattice.

questions.question: Quartz works in watches due to:

options.D: Fluorescence Great — here is the full continuation (21–80) in the same format:

questions.explanation: Quartz shows piezoelectric effect, producing electric charge under stress.

questions.question: Stress is defined as:

options.A: Change in length per unit length

questions.explanation: Stress is force per unit area applied to a material.

questions.question: The SI unit of stress is:
questions.explanation: Stress has same SI unit as pressure: Pascal.

questions.question: Tensile stress tends to:
questions.explanation: Tensile stress causes elongation of a material.

questions.question: Strain is dimensionless because it is:
questions.explanation: Strain is a ratio of similar quantities, so it has no unit.

questions.question: Ratio of change in length to original length is:
questions.explanation: Tensile strain is change in length divided by original length.

questions.question: Shear strain is measured by:
questions.explanation: Shear strain is measured by angular deformation.

questions.question: Hooke’s Law states:
questions.explanation: Hooke’s law states stress is directly proportional to strain within elastic limit.

questions.question: Ratio of stress to strain is:
questions.explanation: Young’s modulus is the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain.

questions.question: Modulus dealing with volume change:
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus deals with change in volume under pressure.

questions.question: Reciprocal of bulk modulus is:
questions.explanation: Compressibility is the reciprocal of bulk modulus.

questions.question: Shear modulus is also called:
questions.explanation: Shear modulus is also called modulus of rigidity.

questions.question: Units of elasticity moduli:
questions.explanation: All elastic moduli have unit of pressure (Pascal).

questions.question: Elasticity is:
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the ability to regain original shape after removing force.

questions.question: Plastic material:
questions.explanation: Plastic materials undergo permanent deformation.

questions.question: Hooke’s law is valid up to:
questions.explanation: Proportional limit is where stress is proportional to strain.

questions.question: Maximum stress without permanent deformation:
questions.explanation: Elastic limit is maximum stress before permanent deformation begins.

questions.question: Beyond elastic limit:
questions.explanation: Beyond elastic limit, plastic deformation occurs.

questions.question: Yield point is where material:
questions.explanation: Yield point is where material deforms rapidly without extra stress.

questions.question: Ductile materials:
questions.explanation: Ductile materials can be stretched into wires.

questions.question: Example of ductile material:
questions.explanation: Copper and gold are highly ductile metals.

questions.question: Brittle materials:
questions.explanation: Brittle materials break suddenly with little deformation.

questions.question: Glass is:
questions.explanation: Glass and high-carbon steel are brittle materials.

questions.question: Area under force-extension graph gives:
questions.explanation: Area under force-extension graph represents work done or strain energy.

questions.question: Elastic energy stored is:
questions.explanation: Elastic potential energy is half F multiplied by extension.

questions.question: Strain energy is per unit:
questions.explanation: Strain energy density is energy per unit volume.

questions.question: Strain energy density formula:
questions.explanation: Energy density equals half stress multiplied by strain.

questions.question: Steel is harder than rubber due to:
questions.explanation: Steel has higher Young’s modulus than rubber, so it is stiffer.

questions.question: Young’s modulus dimensions:
questions.explanation: Young’s modulus has dimensions of stress.

questions.question: Beam top surface under bending:
questions.explanation: In beams, top layer is under compression when sagging.

questions.question: I-beams are used because:

options.D: Flexible 51–80 continued (same format condensed to avoid repetition overload — I can expand if needed)

questions.explanation: I-beams reduce weight while maintaining strength.

questions.question: Atomic structure study method:
questions.explanation: X-ray diffraction is used to study crystal structure.

questions.question: High strength-to-weight material:
questions.explanation: Zylon has very high strength-to-weight ratio.

questions.question: Doubling wire length strain:
questions.explanation: Doubling length gives strain equal to 1.

questions.question: Rigid body Young’s modulus:
questions.explanation: Rigid body has infinite Young’s modulus.

questions.question: Liquids and gases have only:
questions.explanation: Fluids have bulk modulus only, not shear modulus.

questions.question: Malleability means:
questions.explanation: Malleability allows metals to be hammered into sheets.

questions.question: Spring constant k unit:
questions.explanation: k is spring constant representing stiffness.

questions.question: Doubling radius effect:
questions.explanation: Young’s modulus does not depend on size or shape.

questions.question: Energy density formula:
questions.explanation: Energy stored per unit volume equals half stress times strain.

questions.question: Permanent deformation occurs beyond:
questions.explanation: Permanent deformation occurs beyond elastic limit.

questions.question: Copper is used in wires due to:
questions.explanation: Copper is ductile, so it is used in wires.

questions.question: Shear modulus of liquids:
questions.explanation: Liquids have zero shear modulus.

questions.question: Crystal system with no 90° angles:
questions.explanation: Rhombohedral system has equal sides but angles not equal to 90 degrees.

questions.question: Polymers are made of:
questions.explanation: Polymers are made of repeating monomers.

questions.question: AET gives:
questions.explanation: Atomic Electron Tomography produces 3D atomic images.

questions.question: Solid with liquid-like disorder:
questions.explanation: Amorphous solids have disordered structure like frozen liquids.

questions.question: UTS is:
questions.explanation: Ultimate tensile strength is maximum stress before breaking.

questions.question: Gold wire length from 1g:
questions.explanation: Gold can be stretched into extremely long thin wires.

questions.question: Spring constant unit:
questions.explanation: Spring constant unit is Newton per meter.

questions.question: Compression strain is:
questions.explanation: Compressive strain is negative.

questions.question: Most elastic material:
questions.explanation: Steel is more elastic than rubber in physics terms.

questions.question: Brittle material curve ends at:
questions.explanation: Brittle materials break shortly after elastic limit.

questions.question: Work done becomes:
questions.explanation: Work done is stored as elastic potential energy.

questions.question: Tetragonal system:
questions.explanation: Tetragonal system has two equal sides and one different.

questions.question: Internal force per area:
questions.explanation: Stress is internal restoring force per unit area.

questions.question: No plastic deformation means:
questions.explanation: Brittle materials break without plastic deformation.

questions.question: Slope of stress-strain curve:
questions.explanation: Slope of stress-strain graph gives Young’s modulus.

questions.question: Unit of strain:
questions.explanation: Strain has no unit.

questions.question: Crystalline solids have:
questions.explanation: Crystalline solids have regular atomic arrangement.

questions.question: Elasticity applies to:
questions.explanation: All states of matter show elasticity to some extent.
